commitResults.messageTitle: Document student programming and IntelliJ experience
Rename chatbot from Duke to Nova
commitResults.messageBody: Align the entry-point class, startup banner, and user documentation with the selected product name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Nova's initial greeting and farewell
commitResults.messageBody: Present a clearly separated startup message, introduce Nova to the user, and exit with a friendly farewell while keeping the README example aligned.
Read commands from standard input so Nova can echo user input and remain interactive until the user enters bye.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add in-memory task storage and listing
commitResults.messageBody: Store user-entered tasks for the duration of the session and support listing them in insertion order. This completes the Level-2 chatbot behavior without introducing persistence.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for marking tasks as done
commitResults.messageBody: Track completion state alongside each in-memory task, show status markers when listing tasks, and validate mark commands so invalid task numbers do not terminate the chatbot.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for unmarking completed tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Allow users to restore a task to not-done status while preserving task-number validation and the existing in-memory design.

commitResults.messageTitle: Introduce Task model for task state
commitResults.messageBody: Encapsulate each task's description, completion state, state transitions, and display formatting in a dedicated Task class. Refactor Nova to manage Task objects instead of parallel arrays.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add reusable console UI regression testing
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce a repository-scoped test-ui skill with a deterministic fail-fast runner and documented baseline cases. Require agents to maintain the UI plan and run the skill after code changes so console behavior remains verified.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add inherited task types for todos, deadlines, and events
commitResults.messageBody: Model specialized task formatting through Task subclasses and parse each command while retaining string-based dates. Extend console regression coverage for adding, listing, marking, and unmarking all supported task types.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add specific exception handling for invalid commands
commitResults.messageBody: Route malformed task commands and task-number errors through NovaException so users receive actionable correction guidance without terminating the chatbot. Expand console regression coverage for empty, unknown, and incomplete inputs.

Replace the fixed-size task array with a dynamic collection so tasks can be removed cleanly. Add delete command validation and UI regression coverage for removal, renumbering, and invalid task numbers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Model Nova commands with an enum
commitResults.messageBody: Represent the fixed command set and its argument policies with CommandType, then dispatch commands through an enum switch. This centralizes command recognition while preserving the existing console behavior.

Rewrite the task data file after every list mutation so additions, completion changes, and deletions are preserved on disk. Add an exact UI regression check for the serialized task data while leaving loading for the next increment.
Reconstruct todos, deadlines, events, and completion states from the persisted task file when Nova starts. Isolate UI test data in temporary directories and add coverage for loading every task type.

Validate stored task records, escape separator characters, and report read or write failures without crashing. Use safe replacement writes and roll back in-memory mutations when persistence fails, with UI coverage for corrupted data and storage failures.
Build the task data path from OS-independent components, keep save operations relative to the working directory, and verify that Nova creates a missing data directory and file on first use.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add typed scheduling and date-based task search
commitResults.messageBody: Parse deadline and event dates into LocalDateTime values so invalid dates are rejected, display and storage formats stay consistent, and users can find scheduled tasks with the on command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge Level 8 date and time support
commitResults.messageBody: Integrate typed deadline and event scheduling plus date-based task search while retaining a distinct feature-branch history.

Move command input, separators, greetings, errors, and task response formatting out of Nova so the application coordinator no longer depends directly on console APIs. This establishes the UI responsibility required by the OOP design while deliberately preserving all existing command and persistence behavior.

Move command recognition, task construction, date parsing, marker validation, and task-number validation out of Nova. Keep CommandType focused on matching its own keyword form so Parser owns user-command errors and Nova can concentrate on coordinating parsed commands with the UI, storage, and task mutations.

Replace Nova's raw ArrayList with a TaskList that owns ordered access, insertion, deletion, completion changes, immutable snapshots, and date-based searches. Keep save coordination and rollback in Nova so TaskList remains focused on in-memory collection behavior, while Ui receives already-filtered numbered results instead of querying task dates itself.

Replace static collaborators and helper methods with instance fields, constructor-based task loading, and a run method. Retain startup load failures until run begins so the greeting and error order remain unchanged, while main is reduced to constructing Nova with its data path and starting the command loop.

Add an abstract Command protocol with execute and isExit behavior, then route the list operation through a concrete ListCommand. This establishes the polymorphic command boundary in a small step while leaving parsing, mutating commands, persistence rollback, and exit-loop behavior unchanged for later increments.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract find and exit command behavior
commitResults.messageBody: Add FindCommand for date-based task queries and ExitCommand for farewell and loop termination. Change Nova to stop through Command.isExit, and move the final divider into the common loop path so exit behavior is polymorphic while console output remains unchanged.

Add AddCommand to own task insertion, persistence, failed-save rollback, and confirmation output for todos, deadlines, and events. Remove Nova's add helper so the coordinator now delegates the complete add operation through the shared Command execution protocol.

Add MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand on a shared TaskStatusCommand template that owns status mutation, persistence, failed-save restoration, and confirmation dispatch. Remove Nova's status helper so mark and unmark now execute entirely through polymorphic command objects without duplicating rollback logic.

Add DeleteCommand to own task removal, persistence, failed-save reinsertion at the original index, and confirmation output. Remove Nova's final mutation helper so every supported operation now has a Command representation, preparing Parser to become the sole command factory.

commitResults.messageTitle: Defer task existence checks to commands
commitResults.messageBody: Add a shared TaskCommand base that resolves user-facing task numbers against the TaskList during execution. Simplify Parser to validate only missing and non-numeric task numbers, and update mark, unmark, and delete commands to retain one-based numbers so command construction no longer depends on live application state.

Add Parser.parse to construct every concrete Command from a complete input line, keeping command recognition and argument parsing behind one public entry point.

Reduce Nova's run loop to parse, execute, and inspect isExit, while using finally for the trailing divider. This completes the command-pattern coordinator design without changing EOF or console behavior.
Integrate the incremental OOP refactoring that separates UI, storage, parsing, task-list management, and command execution while preserving Nova's console behavior.
Group classes by responsibility to make the project structure easier to navigate and maintain. Update launch documentation and the UI test runner for the packaged main class.
Point the application plugin at nova.Nova so Gradle can launch the renamed and packaged application.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add focused JUnit coverage for core logic
commitResults.messageBody: Test parsing, persistence, date handling, task selection, and command rollback so the highest-value behavior is protected. Document the 50% high-value method coverage target for future code changes.
Name the Shadow artifact nova.jar, preserve service-provider metadata for bundled dependencies, and document how to build, locate, and run it with Java 25.
Add an executable Nova fat JAR configuration and document how students can build and run the packaged application.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete Javadoc coverage for public API
commitResults.messageBody: Document all non-private declarations and non-trivial private helpers so the generated API reference is complete and warning-free.

Bring the production sources in line with the project's basic and
intermediate SE-EDU conventions.

The cleanup standardizes names, switch indentation, constant prefixes,
and Javadoc punctuation while preserving application behavior.

Mandate the skill for future Java changes so production and test code

Add a styled JavaFX chat window that reuses Nova's existing command execution and persistence logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions for internal task invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Several model and command paths rely on values that have already been
validated, but those assumptions are implicit. Violations can therefore
surface later as less informative failures.

Document the parser, index, storage, and task-model invariants with Java
assertions. Keep user-input and persistence validation as normal exception
paths because assertions can be disabled at runtime.

Add focused tests that exercise representative invariant violations while
assertions are enabled.

Date and description searches repeat the same indexed traversal and task
number preservation logic. Maintaining separate copies risks
inconsistent numbering when another search mode is added or one loop
changes.

Route both searches through one predicate-based helper so selection
criteria remain separate while traversal and numbering have one source
of truth.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Make the load path prominent
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage loading nests normal line parsing inside blank-line and
exception branches. That makes the successful path harder to scan and
mixes file iteration with error-context construction.

Use a guard clause for blank lines and move line-specific validation
errors to a dedicated helper. This keeps load's main flow at one
abstraction level while preserving the original diagnostics.

CommandType defines each command keyword, but Parser repeats the same
literals to remove prefixes and label task-number errors. A keyword
change can therefore leave recognition and argument parsing
inconsistent.

Make CommandType provide its keyword and extract matching arguments. Use
named constants for structural markers so parser operations no longer
depend on unexplained string literals.

Task fields are protected even though subclasses never access them
directly.  This exposes mutable completion state more broadly than
necessary and allows descriptions to be reassigned after construction.

Keep both fields private and make descriptions final. Task's existing
methods remain the single place that reads or changes its state,
reducing accidental coupling without changing the public API.

make that programming error explicit.

This follows the defensive branching guideline and gives maintainers a
focused diagnostic.

parsing, completion restoration, and event-range checks in one long
method.  Readers must track several abstraction levels and branching
rules at once.

Separate validation and type construction into focused helpers. Keep the
orchestrating method short so the storage format's processing order is
clear and each helper has one purpose.

Integrate the Assertions increment while retaining the independent
code quality refactorings. This keeps the parallel branch current with
the merged work on master before its pull request is merged.

Integrate the CodeQuality increment while retaining the stream-based
task searches. This keeps the remaining parallel branch current with
the work already merged into master.
TaskList: Use streams for task searches

Use platform-native line separators in response and storage assertions.
This prevents valid Windows output from failing tests solely because it
uses CRLF instead of LF.

Allow users to update one task detail without deleting and recreating
the item. Preserve its type, completion status, list position, and
unspecified data.

Support time-only deadline and event edits while retaining the
existing date. Keep saves transactional and the storage format
backward compatible.

Document the command and cover its parsing, validation, persistence,
rollback, and console behavior with automated tests.

Integrate partial task editing into the main release line. This lets
users change one item detail while preserving its remaining state and
keeps saved data compatible with earlier versions.
